transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

From what you have described, the most likely cause is property socket / supply / switched fused spur. Next: Check the socket works with another appliance and that any separate switched/fused spur controlling it is on (especially after a recent move). Let me know what you find.
the kettle works in the kitchen so the sockets are ok. whats a spur? i dont know what that is sorry

A spur (or "fused spur") is a wall switch with its own fuse that some kitchen appliances are wired through, often found above the worktop and sometimes labelled with the appliance's name. It lets you cut power to a machine that sits behind the counter without pulling it out to reach the plug. Next: Check the plug is fully seated and the lead undamaged - vibration can work a plug loose over time. Let me know what you find.
i cant reach the plug, its behind the machine and its built in so i cant pull it out. im not allowed to take the cupboard off either and i dont have any tools
Next: A blown plug fuse is a clue - the underlying cause needs finding; do not just keep replacing fuses, and leave electrical testing to a professional. Let me know what you find.
ok so what should i do then? i cant check the plug
Next: If there was a pop/bang/burning smell, or any sign of burnt wiring, stop using it and unplug it. Let me know what you find.
no bang or burning smell, nothing like that. its just totally dead. is there anything else i can look at?
Is it completely dead with no lights or display at all, or does it power up and let you choose a programme but then not start?
completely dead, no lights or display at all. nothing comes on when i press the power button
Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?
it was working fine 2 days ago, then this morning its just dead when i press the power button. no sound or anything

From what you have described, the most likely cause is power cord / plug / lead seated and undamaged. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
